candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12 / PDF p.16
candidate.educational_objective: Explain the labeled prolonged, relatively constant pharmacokinetic profile of insulin glargine without overclaiming comparative clinical outcomes.

options.A: Its serum concentration profile is relatively constant and prolonged over about 24 hours
options.B: It has no glucose-lowering effect after injection
options.C: It acts for only about 2 hours and then stops
options.D: It must be mixed with another insulin to develop an effect

candidate.rationale: The LANTUS label describes slower, more prolonged absorption and a relatively constant concentration/time profile over 24 hours with no pronounced peak compared with NPH insulin.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Insulin glargine has slower prolonged absorption and a relatively constant concentration/time profile over 24 hours with no pronounced peak versus NPH.
candidate.stem: A client asks what clinicians mean when insulin glargine is described as having “no pronounced peak.” Which explanation is most accurate?

warning: Technical candidate selection only. This file is not clinical audit evidence and does not establish PASS or FAIL.
